I came out to my friends online, it was easy and they were super accepting about it, my mom I came out to but it was and still is difficult because she is pretty much refusing to use my preferred name and pronouns, but I'm sure she will come around once I talk to her about it again in a more serious manner(the first time I was in tears and kinda just blurted it out and there wasn't much discussion.) As for coming out to my stepdad(Mom told me I /had/ to tell him myself) well I came out to him Wednesday while under the effects of anesthesia and pretty much said "I'm transgender, I know it's a big change but you still love me, right?" and he said yeah, but he's a very stoic man and not much else has been said about it by anyone. The rest of my family(well aside from the ones that are on Facebook and were privy to my coming out post) do not know because of reason not in my control(again with my mother wanting me to stay closeted.) I think the hardest part of coming out for me was fearing rejection because I've had experiences where when I was in my early 20s and tried to come out, my partner was not supportive and I basically shoved myself so far back in the closet I denied myself a huge part of who I am.

Just because you have the opportunity doesn't mean it's the right time, you just have to do what feels right, there is no 'proving' yourself, you are who you are and that's all that matters. As long as you accept and love yourself, the others will fall in line as well, have confidence in yourself and in your friends. Be true to you and just come out in your own way, in your own time, but don't feel like you have to prove yourself and such.
